variables.name: unicast_send_available
variables.description: The messaging service offers an operation for sending a unicast message to a specified address.

variables.name: unicast_received
variables.description: The selected unicast message is received in the selected symbolic occurrence.

variables.name: receiving_address
variables.description: Opaque identity of the receiving address for that same selected message; only equality has meaning.

variables.name: specified_address
variables.description: Opaque identity of that selected message's specified destination address; only equality has meaning.

variables.name: ttl_configuration_available
variables.description: The messaging service offers an operation for configuring multicast message TTL, defined as hop count.

abstraction.subject: messaging service
abstraction.operation: Send a unicast message to its specified address
abstraction.meaning: The source-required unicast sending function must be available.
abstraction.scope: Availability of the named messaging function; no particular invocation is asserted.
limitations: No deployed implementation or successful execution is established.
No delivery, timing, numeric range or network failure semantics is introduced.

abstraction.meaning: If this selected message is received, its receiving address must match its specified address.
abstraction.scope: One symbolic reception occurrence and two opaque address identities referring to the same message.
limitations: Receipt is not required to occur; no eventual delivery, order or history guarantee is established.
This declares an address-equality abstraction; concrete endpoint mapping and implementation realization remain outside the example.

abstraction.subject: messaging service
abstraction.operation: Configure the multicast message TTL hop count
abstraction.meaning: The source-required TTL configuration function must be available; TTL is a hop count, not elapsed time.
abstraction.scope: Availability of the named messaging function; no particular invocation is asserted.
limitations: No deployed implementation or successful execution is established.
No delivery, timing, numeric range or network failure semantics is introduced.
